gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Noto Sans Grantha has tall little letters and bowls that stay wide enough never to snag your eye. Junegull skims along with one unchanging stroke and pinched curves, while the body font keeps the reading smooth.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-gujarat:
Retro, friendly, and built like cast iron.

Junegull's closed curves give way to Noto Sans Gujarati, whose open a, e and s keep a long page of text light and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-gunjala: Junegull looks drawn with a single pen tip, every stroke the same width and every curve pinched nearly shut. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi then loosens things, its cut-back terminals leaving big gaps that let a long passage move along without a snag.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-gurmukh: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads cleanly, with outward-pointing terminals and ascenders that barely rise above the x-height. Junegull's no-modulation outlines make a sturdy partner.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of its height with lowercase and keeps its terminals open, so text feels easy to take in. Junegull, in contrast, bends its strokes like thin plastic tubing into closed loops, and a larger size lets that quality show.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Junegull is the retro, friendly one up top, its stroke never changing and its curves pinched almost shut. Noto Sans Hebrew does the quiet work, with a big midsection and wide gaps.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-hk: Friendly and a little retro, Junegull bends what looks like thin steel rod into every letter, with curves pinched nearly closed. Noto Sans HK lifts its brush ends away before any curve closes, so the text beneath stays open.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-imperia: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic has a c with ends splayed like open pincers. Junegull gives you a constant-width outline you can trace with a finger, and its pinched curves make a lively contrast with that open body.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-inscrip: Friendly and retro, Junegull builds stems like dowels and arcs like bent dowels, each curve pinched nearly shut. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian answers with big open eyes on every e and a, and a deep middle band that lets the text breathe.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Noto Sans Kaithi has an open channel in its e and lowercase that fills the line almost like capitals. Over many paragraphs it stays easy and uncrowded.
